f.title: Comply with the national pharmacovigilance system established by the Authority
f.statement: The Pharmacy and Medicines Regulatory Authority establishes and maintains a national pharmacovigilance system with which all marketing authorizations, as determined by the Authority, shall comply. Through that system the Authority monitors and analyses adverse effects or events, monitors clinical trials and takes regulatory action; mandatory industry reporting and periodic safety updates are to be provided for by regulations under section 72(3).
f.clause: Part VI, section 72. Establishment of national pharmacovigilance system
f.applicability: All medicines and allied substances with a marketing authorization, as determined by the Authority
f.exceptions: The detailed reporting duties (industry adverse event reporting, periodic safety updates) are left to regulations made by the Minister under section 72(3); none are stated in the Act.

f.title: Principal investigator submits prescribed end-of-trial reports to the Authority
f.statement: At the end of a clinical trial, the principal investigator shall submit to the Authority a copy of the prescribed reports of the clinical trial; the Minister may prescribe their contents and format by Gazette notice. The Authority monitors and inspects clinical trial sites during the trial.
f.clause: Part VII, section 77. Monitoring, inspection and reporting of clinical trial
f.applicability: Clinical trials under a clinical trial certificate

f.title: Dispose of recalled medicines as directed; manufacturer or importer bears recall costs
f.statement: Where the Authority recalls a medicine or allied substance because its availability is not in the public interest, no person shall dispose of it contrary to the manner prescribed by the Authority. The cost of recall and disposal is borne by the local manufacturer (locally manufactured products), the importer (foreign manufactured products), or another person determined by the Authority case by case. Contravention is an offence.
f.clause: Part VI, section 69. Recall of medicine etc., from circulation
